claims.claim: The tests show gains over the original EBEN, including a 40-person MUSHRA comparison; the authors report clearer high-frequency detail and less distortion.
claims.limitations: French LibriSpeech, sampling setup, listeners, and author-reported metrics bound the result; other languages remain open.

claims.claim: The paper reports higher fidelity and naturalness than listed baselines and MOSA 3.38.
claims.limitations: Dataset, subjects, protocol, learned evaluator, and paper-reported comparisons limit clinical claims.

claims.claim: Audio-based adaptation gives the largest reported gains across tested conditions.
claims.limitations: Sound set, target examples, class construction, and reported accuracy limit open-world claims.

claims.claim: Results suggest prosodic mispronunciation inhibits recognition at the tested delay.
claims.limitations: Japanese materials, pitch-accent system, participants, and laboratory task limit cross-language generalization.

claims.claim: Curriculum and anchoring lower PER and improve speaker similarity across reported groups.
claims.limitations: Groups, language, recording conditions, and reported metrics limit clinical claims.

claims.claim: Model size improves ASR thresholds, but the gap changes with language, room, and spatial signals.
claims.limitations: Whisper versions, German/English material, steady noise, and laboratory setup limit claims.

claims.claim: The system is competitive with challenge baselines and identifies languages needing targeted work.
claims.limitations: Challenge data, language mix, averaging, and tuning limit all-multilingual claims.

claims.claim: Sound errors have higher transcription accuracy than word errors, with position-dependent differences.
claims.limitations: Database, annotations, WhisperX, language, and task design limit generalization.
